patterns.usage_note: Rising-intonation だって: you throw back what you have just heard and ask the hearer to confirm it (校庭だって？ "on the field, is it?"), so it belongs to a question turn rather than to a plain report. It comes from the quotative って on the copula だ and so rides on nouns; in real speech it equally follows the explanatory ん (行くんだって？), an attachment this corpus rule does not license. The same string said on a falling tone is the sibling hearsay use that simply passes the news along (中止だって。); only this checking use invites an answer. ですって is the polite variant and reads as feminine in most speech. Do not confuse it with the homophonous sentence-initial だって "because" or the 〜だって "even/also" of 子供だって知っている.

examples.ruby: 明日[あした]の練習[れんしゅう]、体育館[たいいくかん]じゃなくて校庭[こうてい]だって？
examples.english: Tomorrow's practice is out on the field, not in the gym — that right?

examples.ruby: 隣[となり]の田中[たなか]さん、春[はる]には引[ひ]っ越[こ]しだって？
examples.english: The Tanakas next door are moving out in the spring, is that right?

examples.ruby: え、あの二人[ふたり]、来月[らいげつ]には離婚[りこん]だって？
examples.english: Wait, you're telling me those two are getting divorced next month?
